title: Low-Dose Programmable Scanning Patterns for Correlative Ptychography and EELS in Ferroelectric Thin Films
content: Understanding phase transitions in ferroelectric thin films is critical for advancing both fundamental research and technological applications. These transitions often involve subtle atomic displacements and changes in polarization states, which directly affect the stability, switching dynamics, and retention of functional properties in memory storage, energy harvesting, and quantum information devices [1]. Tracking the atomic displacements within the unit cell provides essential insights into symmetry-breaking processes, domain wall formation, and topological configurations such as vortex structures, all of which are key to controlling and engineering material behaviour at the atomic scale [2]. Conventional real space transmission electron microscopy (TEM) imaging techniques fall short of capturing the 3D nature of the changes in symmetry of ferroelectric interfaces such as domain walls and vortices. It is essential to develop techniques that can capture the 3D atomic displacements and thus polarisation patterns of such functional interfaces [3].
